basic_info: 55-year-old male presenting with lower back pain; history of prior discectomy
present_illness: Onset five days ago during heavy lifting (moving refrigerator); localized to lower right back. The pain is in the lower right back and hurts when bending over. No numbness, tingling, or weakness in the legs. Pain intensity is 6 or 7 out of 10. The pain feels worse when bending over or moving in the way that caused the injury, and it does not improve much with rest. No other symptoms. The patient has been taking ibuprofen and once tried Tylenol and ibuprofen together, which gave some relief.
past_history: Previous discectomy (location: unspecified, timing: unspecified, outcome: unspecified). Patient reports no recurrence or complications following the surgery.
physical_exam: Physical examination findings: Tenderness localized to the lower right back. No neurological deficits noted (no numbness, tingling, or weakness in the legs). Range of motion limited due to pain, particularly with bending over. No signs of neurological involvement.
aux_exam: Patient reports no imaging studies for the current lower back pain yet. The doctor mentioned looking at an X-ray and some labs, but the results are not known. An MRI is planned to be sure.
